title: Progressive exposure manifest and rollback heuristics
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define and implement a declarative 'progressive exposure manifest' and the associated rollback heuristics used by the deployment controller. The manifest should describe fractional exposure steps (percentages and cohorts), shadow sampling configuration for offline validation, A/B allocations, and escalation windows. The heuristics engine must evaluate streaming telemetry and decide automated pauses, rollbacks, or escalation to human operators using a combination of statistical tests and business-rule thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema v1 documented and validated against examples
Controller can execute a 5-step exposure plan and report progress to Console
Automatic rollback triggers fire under defined conditions in CI-simulated noise and injected-failure tests
Shadow traffic sampling is configurable per-manifest and visible in telemetry dashboards
A/B allocations can be specified alongside shadow and preserve identity routing when requested
Unit and e2e tests cover at least 90% of decision branches in heuristics module
technical_notes: Design will use a two-layer approach: 1) Declarative manifest (YAML/JSON) mapping steps -> {percent, cohort_selector, duration, stability_checks}; 2) Heuristics engine that evaluates metrics (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, model-quality regression score) and runs a lightweight sequential test (CUSUM + exponential moving baseline). For model-quality checks we'll integrate with Evaluate service via /evals/ingest. Heuristics will emit structured decisions (CONTINUE/PAUSE/ROLLBACK/ESCALATE) with reason codes for audit.

rollout_plan_example: steps: [ {name: 'step-1', pct: 1, duration: '30m', checks: ['error_rate<0.5%','p95<200ms']}, {name: 'step-2', pct: 5, duration: '1h', checks: ['quality_regression<0.5%','latency_stable']}, {name: 'step-3', pct: 20, duration: '2h', checks: ['manual-approval?false','service_error_rate<1%']}, {name: 'step-4', pct: 60, duration: '4h'}, {name: 'final', pct: 100, duration: '0s'} ]
rollback_conditions: Primary triggers: sustained error-rate > configured threshold for window (default 3x baseline for 10 minutes), quality regression above user-defined delta (absolute or percentile based), p95 latency spikes > 2x baseline OR anomaly score > 0.8 from the streaming detector. Secondary triggers: missing telemetry for a step (eg telemetry ingestion lag > 2x), or health-check drops below 90%. When triggered, heuristics escalate to: (1) immediate rollback when severity==critical, (2) pause + retry with backoff for medium, (3) create incident and request manual verification for low. All decisions recorded to audit log with fingerprint and causal metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and validation. Sim harness that replays historical traffic + injected faults to assert expected decision path. e2e test against a test controller environment that runs a synthetic model, exercises shadow traffic and A/B splitter, and asserts rollback path executes. Load test to ensure heuristics evaluation loop can process 10k decisions/min without affecting control-plane latency.
ui_and_api_changes: Console: new 'Exposure' panel showing step state, percentage, cohort heatmap, and top contributing metrics for each step. API: /v1/releases/{id}/exposure-manifest POST/GET. Add audit endpoint to stream decisions to customer-owned sinks for Private deployments.
implementation_notes: Prefer a go-first implementation for controller components to reuse existing runtime routing libs. Heuristics should be a small deterministic library (no external ML models initially) so it's reproducible in Private deployments. Persist manifest and per-step state in the Releases store with optimistic concurrency. Consider future: allow pluggable detectors (python modules) for advanced anomaly detection.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, require multi-metric agreement before auto-rollback, and soft-fallback to pause and gather more samples. Risk: telemetry sparsity for low-volume cohorts. Mitigation: allow absolute-count targets and longer observation windows. Risk: operational complexity for customers. Mitigation: provide template manifests and sensible presets (low-risk, balanced, aggressive).
